source.title: Scalable and Robust LLM Unlearning by Correcting Responses with Retrieved Exclusions
source.authors: Junbeom Kim; Kyuyoung Kim; Jihoon Tack; Dongha Lim; Jin-Woo Shin

page_placements.theme: Recovery baselines: never-trained or retrained references also 'recover', and relearning speed reflects more than retained information

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether unlearning baselines continue to leak under indirect queries and reports that RMU and ECO do, while CURE reduces such leakage. This refines and partly challenges claims that unlearning suppresses access to the target knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates indirect, generalized TOFU queries after unlearning, which bears on prompt-only recovery. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation or analysis, or quantization. Rows below record the TOFU Llama3.1-8B results in Table 6; other reported benchmark results do not test an attack in versions B–E.
record.test_reason: The paper probes unlearned Llama3.1-8B models (GradDiff, DPO, NPO, RMU, prompting, ECO) on TOFU with GPT-4o-generated indirect rephrasings of the forget questions, and reports leakage against target and retain references (Table 6). This is a prompt-only recovery test (E) and bears on whether the methods work (A). It also proposes CURE, an output-correction method it claims resists such leakage (F). It applies no fine-tuning, activation-ablation or quantization attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that RMU and ECO look effective on direct queries but leak substantially under indirect queries, so they merely suppress outputs for specific prompts. They say GradDiff/DPO/NPO reduce leakage only by degrading utility and plausibility. CURE, an output corrector that leaves base weights untouched, reduces indirect leakage by 69.2% relative to the original model while preserving utility, and stays stable under continual unlearning. They also note that retain models can leak through distributional inference.
record.recipe_differences: CURE retrieves exclusions and corrects model outputs using a trained LoRA corrector; it does not apply the claim's fine-tuning recovery, direction-ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery procedures to unlearned weights. The paper also evaluates RMU and other unlearning baselines.
record.method_sensitivity: Leakage differs between direct and indirect/generalized query conditions and across unlearning methods. The authors report that results vary by domain and benchmark as well.

fits_no_version.finding: The retain model, never trained on the forget set, leaks 23.75% on direct and 3.60% on indirect TOFU queries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retain-model 'oracle' references can themselves leak target facts via distributional inference, which complicates leakage baselines.

record.problems: The claim-relevant TOFU results are reported for Llama3.1-8B in Table 6; the paper's TOFU evaluation uses the 10% forget split. Indirect queries were generated using GPT-4o, so this is one constructed prompt-variation setup, not a broad test of rephrasing attacks. Leakage is judged by GPT-4o. No uncertainty estimates are reported in Table 6. The paper states that full reproduction of the original WMDP setup was not possible because its corpus was unavailable.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant rows omitted from Table 6. Other benchmark tables report WMDP and MMLU unlearning performance but do not apply the attacks in versions B–E.

untested.parts: No relearning or fine-tuning attack on any unlearned model.
No activation-direction ablation or mechanistic analysis. The 'suppressed not erased' claim is inferred from indirect-query leakage only.
Only GPT-4o-generated generalized rephrasings on TOFU (fictitious authors). No jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information. No indirect-query test on WMDP/MMLU.

CURE is tested only against indirect queries. It is not tested against fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, jailbreaks or adversarial prompts aimed at the corrector. CURE leaves base weights unchanged by design, so any white-box or weight-access attack is untested and would trivially apply.
Near-chance accuracy in the WMDP sense is not tested with the original WMDP corpus; the authors say full reproduction was impossible.

missing.what: Continual unlearning over 20 requests. RMU shows nearly 40% leakage under indirect queries with utility ~75%; NPO collapses. Only shown in a figure, no numbers table.

WMDP/MMLU on Zephyr-7B. NPO/RMU/ECO reach near-zero WMDP EM, but validity is only 1.6-16.9%, so the low accuracy comes from invalid outputs. RMU keeps MMLU at 50.44. Data are QA pairs, not the original WMDP corpus.
MMLU subset unlearning (economics/law/physics). RMU/ECO forget-set EM is low but validity is low; NPO zeroes retain subsets.
Plausibility scores on direct and indirect queries per method (e.g., RMU direct 0.0001).

record.verdict_notes: The indirect-query ceiling is low: the target model leaks only 15.60% on indirect queries vs 98.25% on direct ones. E support therefore means RMU/ECO retain ~90% of a modest leakage level. Leakage is judged by GPT-4o; the text says Maj@5 in one place and Maj@3 in another. There are no uncertainty estimates. CURE is a guardrail-style method whose base weights still hold the knowledge, so its F support applies only to black-box prompting. The text labels the Qwen tables inconsistently (Tables 7/8 vs 9/10).

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures leakage and utility, not whether targeted-knowledge accuracy is near chance in the exact sense stated by the claim. Its indirect-query test covers one kind of prompt attack; it does not test fine-tuning, internal edits, or quantization attacks.
No small-set fine-tuning or relearning attack is applied after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge is reported.
No low-bit quantization attack is applied.
The paper tests indirect/generalized queries on TOFU, not jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
CURE is evaluated under indirect queries, but not against fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
